source: No kernel counterpart. The identity the test checks is the bridge's pre-filled fallback in OCCTDocumentExplorerLocation, returned when the walk finds no node at the index; XCAFPrs_DocumentExplorer has no node, and so no location, at index count + 100. The probe confirms the walk: one leaf, and no node reached at index 101. Its last line, the pre-#1480 formula evaluated as plain arithmetic (1.0 at slots 0, 5, 6, 11), is not a kernel output and is no longer carried in kernel_output.

test_name: Document Layers::Document has XCAF built-in layers

differences: layer_count_positive: the bridge side is true, the kernel's layer table gives false. The bridge calls XCAFDoc_LayerTool::Set(Main), which attaches a layer tool to the main label 0:1 and lists that label's three children as layers (Shapes at 0:1:1, Colors at 0:1:2, VisMaterials at 0:1:10), where the document's own layer table, XCAFDoc_DocumentTool::LayerTool(Main) on LayersLabel() 0:1:3, holds 0 layers on a fresh document.
names_non_empty: true on the bridge side, false in the kernel's layer table, for the same reason: the three names are the XCAF tool labels, not layers.
This is a defect, not a design choice: the test asserts it (a fresh document has layers). Tracked as #2413; the fix is in Sources/ and is not part of this PR.

source: Same quantities on both sides: whether the fresh document reports any layer and any layer name. Bridge: the test observed layerCount > 0 and layerNames non-empty (OCCTDocumentGetLayerCount / OCCTDocumentGetLayerName read XCAFDoc_LayerTool::Set(Main)). Kernel: the document's layer table, XCAFDoc_DocumentTool::LayerTool(Main) at 0:1:3, has 0 layer labels on a fresh document, so both are false; the same probe shows the bridge's own call returning 3 labels (Shapes, Colors, VisMaterials). The values differ because of #2413, so this is recorded as a divergence and not as a pass. Kernel values are from the probe named in the record, which makes the same calls the bridge makes.

test_name: Document Layers::Layer name out of range returns nil
source: Same quantities on both sides: whether a layer name exists at index 999 and at index -1. Bridge: layerName(at: 999) and layerName(at: -1) were both nil (OCCTDocumentGetLayerName returns -1 for an index outside 0..<labels.Length()). Kernel: on the sequence the bridge reads (XCAFDoc_LayerTool::Set(Main), 3 labels), Value(1000) and Value(0), the 1-based positions for those indices, both raise Standard_OutOfRange, so no name can be read at either. The result does not depend on #2413: any label count below 1000 gives the same. Kernel values are from the probe named in the record, which makes the same calls the bridge makes.
